review:
So I've fairly run out of things to do in only 13 hours.. got a few achievements left to clear but here's my thoughts on this...

If I was able to refund this, I would.   Sorry, but the only collectable resources in the product are as follows:

Resources: Wood planks, sticks, rocks, cloth, fertilizer and seeds (also potato plants).
Food: Cans 3 types, water, soda energy bars (2 types) and potatoes.
Guns: 5 types but you can't seem to craft your own bullets, you need to get them off soldier bodies and even then its 1-17 (mostly on the lower end)
Two types of animals: pigs and chickens and they don't seem to die of starvation at all if you don't feed them.
The buildings...... man all I can say is its literally the most BASIC of building models...    foundation, wall, door, door frame, window, fence, gate, stair and defense walls (which break as easily as falling over a banana peel)... zombies just smash those with no real deterant. 
Only the spikes are any value for defense and those last a little longer.

there's 14 collectable blueprints - that's it.   2-3 machines (fertilizer, biofuel and one other), 3 crop planting blocks 1x3.2x3 and 3x3.  Then its a few weapons (iron axe, iron shovel, iron pickaxe, iron mace, iron spear, machete), a few other minor things like bear trap, metal crate... but overall the recipes are a huge disappointment. Then lastly like 3 upgrades to your car, which drives pretty badly anyhow regarding control.

Three odd quests only which only unlock access to the traders.

You can make one portable workbench which literally only crafts the basics.  The other two workbenches you repair in the garage lets you do the construction buildables (walls, foundations, etc) and the other for the collectable blueprints you find.  But you can't build those workbenches anywhere else... you can only use those in that garage which is at the corner of the map.. so long-a$$ run back and forth if you want to build anything anywhere else.

My overall experience is that this game is literally an asset base package.   Its far, far, far from being a survival game as there's literally barely anything in product except the bare bones of an idea.   At present with its status I would give this a wide berth until there's actually content, because I would not even flag it as replayable.  
Its not abandoned (at least from the posts I've seen), but I certainly cannot justify the $18 price tag when I've bought games for half that with tons more content and certainly are replayable.
I had hopes for this when I saw it and at the time I purchased it, reviews were still positive.  Unsurprising how its already flipped to mixed in a short time of when I bought this.

review:
Alright. [i]The Last FARMER[/i] is a game that released a few weeks ago and is this devs version of a survival game set in a zombie post apocalypse. And it is better than a lot of its Unity store contemporaries. It does however also have quite a few issues that had me double checking just to verify that it wasn't in early access. Because while it is a mostly feature complete game, there are some frustrations that probably could have been ironed out more easily if it WAS in early access. Also, if you scroll down to the purchase part of the product page, it says it is called [i]FARMER SIMULATOR[/i]. And I think that oversight is emblematic of some of the other fairly obvious issues that hopefully also will be fairly uncomplicated to resolve.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3362953036

The story set-up is pretty straightforward. You are a dude who has been scraping by in the post apocalypse, but now you're looking for a place to settle in and simplify life by becoming a farmer. Of course, in order to do so, you will have to fortify the place you find (an old auto shop) and expand it so you can grow crops and hopefully raise livestock. Nothing in life is simple though and the remnants of the area's military have adopted a protection racket, wherein you pay them every few days in produce in order to be protected from them, lol. And from what I can tell, the main story will have you overthrow said group. There not a lot of story and the actual voice acted dialogue where it exists has a fair few comically mispronounced words. Additionally, there are weird gaps after every apostrophe in the notes you find. Such as "it'   s".

You will spend most of your time crafting and exploring with combat interludes. The crafting is all pretty intuitive and will feel familiar to anybody who has played a game featuring such. Nothing crazy there, and it works fine, although the fact that using up an item crafting something doesn't register as having an open inventory slot is a minor issue. All crafted tools have item degradation. Not my favorite gameplay mechanic, but it's not too invasive here. You also have the opportunity to fix up a car and then repair said car after you inevitably run over enough zombies and soldiers to damage it. The car is fun enough to drive, although the game will at times stutter while driving.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3363555060

You will be relying heavily on crafted spears and clubs for combat. Which also have quality degradation as you use them. Clubs are more powerful, but I'd argue they are pretty useless because they have short arm reach and you will be trading with zombies more often than not. They can be effective against soldiers, but there's really zero reason to use clubs when spears are an option. And spears do have the same short arm issue, but the weapon is long enough to where a simple kite and then attack while moving backwards technique works against all zombie types. You can also find firearms. I have only ever found assault rifles. They don't have quality degradation, but ammo is fairly limited and the bullets don't do much damage, so you will waste a fair few on each enemy. A nice thing is the audio when you hit an enemy is different than when you miss, giving you a better indication of when you actually hit something. 

Two issues with firearms beyond the low damage. First off, bullet stacking doesn't work properly in your inventory. Any bullets you add to your already existing stack will not register as being in your inventory for the purposes of reloading your weapon. The only way to circumvent this issue is to split the stack repeatedly until it does register the bullets. The second issue is that for some reason, they have zero monetary value at traders. Which is pretty sucky.

In fact, outside of limited cap value for craftable items, which you aren't going to want to sell, you can only sell food/water/gasoline. All of which you definitely should be trying to hold onto. In fact, from what I can tell, the only item actually worth taking to traders is cooked pumpkin, which gives you 100 caps per. The entire trader system needs to be overhauled IMO. The items they have that you might need are waaaaayyyy overpriced, but you get comparatively nothing when you sell similar items.

Exploration feels pretty good, be it on foot or in your vehicle. However, there are really only a few variations of buildings and there is a lot of space between them. And most building only really spawn seeds, soda, and canned food. And actually, outside of food, craftables, seeds, and occasionally bottle caps, there really isn't any loot to speak of. Very very rarely, you will find a gasoline can.

Some of the building are also unfinished and you will fall through ceilings or floors periodically. And sometimes, you can't get back out because the stairs that are inevitably there are only there visually. You will just walk right through them rather than climb them. Where I stopped playing was when that happened in an actual quest area (The prison cellblock C). There was literally no way to get up the stairs from second to third floor.

Also, default mouse sensitivity is insane. I dropped it down most all the way from whatever it was originally. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3363555045

The thing is, I actually like this game a fair amount. I'd found a few quests that I was wanting to finish. Delivering the occult book to a certain weirdo, finding the photo in the prison, letting an outpost know the military camp had been crushed. But at some point, when the issues stack up, you just gotta call uncle and set it down. I will continue to follow the game and see what the devs do to remedy these issues and any other issues other players have or might report on. It's otherwise a small step above what is a heavily saturated zombie survival game market filled with Unity store assets. I guess they're maybe a bit more proficient using those assets.

 For now, my recommendation would be to hold off on buying it but to give the game a follow and watch how bug fixes and polish updates come through. I will be giving this a thumbs down here due to the lack of a neutral option and the abundance of issues, but via curation, it will receive an informational rating instead.

review:
[h2][b][u]Note:[/u][/b][/h2]
 This is a review originally written for [url= https://www.opiumpulses.com] Opium Pulses [/url]. The full article can be found [url= https://www.opiumpulses.com/article/869/the-last-farmer-review] HERE [/url]. Feel free to take a look at the Opium Pulse Steam Curation page [url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/3800356/] HERE [/url] as well.

The Last Farmer is a survival/horror game by developer Geekon. What will be the developers 15th game release within a year-and a half, one might be slightly pensive as to what sort of quality they’re bringing to the table. If my time spent in-game as well as taking the overwhelmingly trend-specific ratings of prior titles into account: the concerns are entirely well founded. That being said, while there is ABSOLUTELY a market of games that are simply “so bad they’re good”, it seems as though Geekon misses the mark even in that regard. 

Coming-to in a dead-end nook of a desert, your character makes his way to a small overlook, where you find the remnants of a barn, and a conveniently placed natural source of clean water. Within the dilapidated barn, you find a worse-for-wear car (which will turn into a long term project to help aid in your supply runs) and a “conveniently” placed bed, as well as several workstations you’ll need to get up and running to get yourself fully functional for the road ahead, as desolate and clunky as it may be. 
Effectively you’re a farmer in a post-zombie-apocalypse situation, just trying to survive in your “journey of restoration”!

And what a journey it is! Opening strong with poor font spacing during story-board cut scenes and atrocious spelling mistakes within the bare bones tutorial, you’ll be journeying across your keyboard trying to figure out what keys do what. Minimal explanations and no viewable key binding menu, or ability adds to frustrations. While some of the controls feel about par for the industry, the inability to remap or even view them starts players off on a fairly sour note. 

To further add to the magnificently clunky journey, poor optimization, overly sensitive default movement (the default is set to 25, I ended up setting mine to 10 for it to feel “normal”) as well as generally broken setting plague The Last Farmer. Default sound settings end up near muted is the slider is moved more than a few ticks. Music changes suddenly, without warning nor transition, and without any real reason. The audio is bland and uninspired, and grows old quickly.  In addition, the voice acting is relatively bland and awkward, leaving MUCH to be desired. 

As far as visuals go, there is very little to write home about. From your giant Meat Mittens with oddly protruding fingernails to the blatant use of assets slapped left and right, there is not much to see. Picking the barren obscure desert of Texas leave little to be seen, sans randomly placed (and nonsensically designed) homes, abandoned military bases, and odd “points of interest” that have little to be interested in, and seem relatively out of place. In an odd way, it almost feels like the desert was a choice made as an excuse for it to be relatively bare in terms of “filler”. What could have been a relatively promising concept, once again, falls flat.

In a market nearly over saturated in both survival craft as well as zombie titles, you will find plenty of titles that do what is attempted here, but better for near the same cost. While perhaps not hinging on the Farmer aspect as much, games like 7 Days to Die still provide a vastly more entertaining time, and much less frustration. In short, repetitive assets, boring and blurry zombies with the same vocals, uninspired design and just a general lack of effort really make The Last Farmer just about The Last Thing on my list when it comes to Zombie Survival Craft titles.

In it's current state, I just can't recommend it... Yet.
I'll keep this short. Extremely unpolished and bare bones. You find you are trying to convince yourself it's good or to be more patient, which in itself is a bad sign.

No character level ups, no character customisation, No body equipment, no headshot bonus damage in a ZOMBIE game, no limb damage, a forced home base, no zombie spawn control, no tool repairs, TINY storage and stack quantities... I could go on for hours.
I'm hoping to come back and change this review in time but it must be said, I'm skeptical in my expectations of this title. In short, It doesn't seem the devs entirely understand what they were setting out for in this title that completely lacks identity. Is it a farming sim or a zombie survivor? Noone knows.

review:
Can't recommend this game for a few reasons.

First, there's basically nothing to do. It starts off with a grind, you purchase your "properties" in the slums, add a sleeping bag and sell them until you unlock the suburbs. After which it starts to snowball pretty quickly. The "negotiations" consist of figuring out what the max an npc is willing to pay (usually about 150/100/80% profit for low/medium/high priced properties) and set all the properties in that specific range to that price, and just offer to npc's until they agree. You can go through dozens of people before you get a person to pay the price you want, regardless of the price you set it to.

Second, there is absolutely no end game. You have nothing to aim for, other than afford the most expensive property. You by the most expensive house, you sell it, repeat. There's no type of skill upgrade system or competition that would make you keep wanting to play. You get a small boost to some stats as you upgrade through the offices (3 total, your starting one and 2 better ones). But these stats are pretty ambiguous and you really can't tell what they do or if they even work.

Finally, six days before I purchased the game (7 before writing this review), they added a "quirky office intruder" (devs words). This intruder does nothing but walk into your office in his underwear, play some random music on a stereo and no customers will come in until you shoo him away. He adds absolutely nothing to the game. No reward. Not fun. Only annoyance. I got so frustrated dealing with this guy because of the random, yet frequent visits he made, causing the customer that I was about to show the house to walks out right before clicking the offer button.

review:
On paper this should be a great game, a tycoon version of House Flipper? Sign me up. Unfortunately this game fails to live up to it's promise in pretty much every way.  The game is nothing but a grind. Don't get me wrong that can be fun, I've sunk hundreds of hours into grindy games like Destiny, Diablo, the Division, etc. The difference? Those are fun. REAL ESTATE Simulator isn't.

The first hour of the game is just an awful loop where you buy the same tent, shipping container or abandoned school bus and can only "improve" it by adding a sleeping bag. Then you sell it to one of the same 5 or 6 people who all use the exact same male or female voice.  All with the promise of unlocking the suburb and city levels where you can actually buy furniture and change the floors and walls and actually improve the listings.

Guess what? It doesn't get better. Yes, there's a painfully small amount of items you can now buy, but it makes very little difference to the value. And it's clunky. Oh, and you can only buy stuff at your office. Short one piece of flooring to finish your upgrade? You have to go back to the bus stop, sit through a loading screen, buy the missing item, leave your office, sit through another loading screen, catch a cab to the suburbs, sit through another loading screen, walk into the house, sit through another loading screen and then put that last piece of flooring into place.  Are we having fun yet? Welcome to Loading Screen Simulator.

The game has some potential, but in it's present state I'd barely consider it a functional demo.

review:
TLDR: I can't recommend this game.  It had the chance to be great, good even, but it's not.  Get House Flipper instead.

Here's something that will bother the majority of people looking to buy this game:

You HAVE to buy all the items at your office before going to the house.  That's right, you can't take out a tablet and buy furniture or anything at the house, no, you have to go to your office.  So if you forget something or want to see how something looks, sell it, and try something else you have to run back to your office.  And it's not just a quick exit house and you teleport back, no.  You have to walk to the bus stop then walk to the office from the bus stop.  Same way going to the house.  You can't buy a house on your computer and click 'go to house'.  You have to exit office and walk to the bus stop.  
It wastes so much time and it's unnecessary; it annoyed me so much I just gave up on the game.  

Honestly, if you want to buy a house, fix it up, and sell it - just buy House Flipper.  I thought this would be a bit different and it would be it's own thing, but no, it tried to be house flipper but made everything more difficult, longer, and worse.

Okay I don't even know how to start this one and as you can see I've reviewed a lot of games.

It's the poor man's house flipper!

That's pretty much it. This game is not awful, or at least for my playthrough it wasn't. It's just very small, very bland, doesn't have a lot going for it.

Does it have originality? no.
Does it have long playtime? No.
Does it have addictive gameplay? yes.
Does it have great sound or graphics? no.
Does it have intuitive gameplay design/mechanics? No.
Is it worth it's asking price? yes.

It's just like house flipper. You go and buy a house cheap. Fix it up and make it look nice. Then sell it for an expensive price. Rinse and repeat. but it lacks all the options and intuitive gameplay mechanics or design that House Flipper had.

I'd say just pass on this one. Maybe if it had more slice of life aspects or if it had something new and different or a massive game hidden inside I might say it was worth it. but it's just not.
